# Agent mailbox

Two agents in one checkout can overwrite each other. The mailbox is an append-only JSON-lines
file where each agent announces the paths it edits. Any agent that can run a shell command can
use it. The wrapper is `agent-mailbox.mjs` (bundled next to this skill). Below, `<skill-dir>` is the directory this
file sits in, and `<name>` is your own sender name.

```bash
node <skill-dir>/agent-mailbox.mjs claim <name> <path...> [--ttl <hours>] [--force]
node <skill-dir>/agent-mailbox.mjs release <name> [path...]
node <skill-dir>/agent-mailbox.mjs claims
node <skill-dir>/agent-mailbox.mjs send <name> [--to <agent>] '<message>'
node <skill-dir>/agent-mailbox.mjs inbox <name> [--wait <seconds>]
node <skill-dir>/agent-mailbox.mjs read [--last <n>] [--all]
node <skill-dir>/agent-mailbox.mjs watch <name>
node <skill-dir>/agent-mailbox.mjs up <name>[=<command>]...
node <skill-dir>/agent-mailbox.mjs run <name> <command...>
node <skill-dir>/agent-mailbox.mjs shell-init [<agent>...]
node <skill-dir>/agent-mailbox.mjs down [<name>...]
node <skill-dir>/agent-mailbox.mjs dispatch
```

Where the `ethlete-agents` package is a dependency, `npx ethlete-agents mailbox <command>` runs the same script, so you do not need `<skill-dir>`.

Choose a `<name>` that no other agent uses, for example `agent-a` or
`agent-b`. Two sessions with one name look like one agent. For two Claude Code sessions, the
`SendMessage` tool is the better channel. The mailbox is for agents that cannot reach each other
directly.

The file is `.ethlete/mailbox.jsonl` in the git root. The first write also creates
`.ethlete/.gitignore`, so the file stays out of git. Set `AGENT_MAILBOX` to use another path.

## Protocol

1. At the start of a task, run `claims` and `inbox`. They show what other agents hold and said.
2. Before you edit a file, run `claim` with the exact paths. A directory path claims everything
   below it. `claim` also prints the messages you have not seen yet.
3. If `claim` reports a conflict, do not edit. Run `send` to ask the holder for a handoff, then wait.
4. After each larger step, run `inbox` again. Most agents cannot wake on new output, so you must
   pull messages yourself.
5. If you wait for an answer from another agent, do not stop. Run `inbox <name> --wait 120`: it
   blocks until a message arrives or 120 seconds pass. If it prints "No new messages.", run it
   again. Stop the loop only when the task is done or the user tells you to.
6. When you finish, run `release`. A claim also expires after 4 hours, or after `--ttl` hours.

A claim is advisory, not a lock. `--force` claims over another agent: use it only after the
holder agreed. Silence is not approval. Acknowledge each handoff in words.

## Wake an idle agent

An idle agent cannot read the mailbox. One `dispatch` process outside every agent fixes this. It polls the mailbox for free. When a message carries `--to <agent>`, it types a wake-up line into the `tmux` session `<agent>@<repo>`, or a session named only `<agent>`. The agent then runs `inbox` and acts.

1. Run `up` once. `up codex=codex gemini=gemini` starts a detached `tmux` session per agent, named like its sender name, and runs the command in it. It also starts a session named `mailbox-dispatch` that runs `dispatch`. A running session is left alone.
2. Attach to a session with `tmux attach -t <name>`. Detach with `Ctrl-b`, then `d`. The session and its agent keep running.
3. Send a message with `send <name> --to <agent> '<message>'`. A message without `--to` wakes nobody.

If the agent is in the middle of a turn, the wake-up line waits as its next prompt. An agent in a `tmux` session does not need the `--wait` loop, which costs a turn at every timeout.
A background `--wait` also ends after one message, so it is not a lasting watch. Use `down` to stop the sessions.

## Start agents with the plain command

`run <name> <command...>` starts the command in the `tmux` session `<name>@<repo>`, or attaches if it runs already. It also starts the dispatcher when none runs. Session names carry the repo name, so `codex` in two repos never collides. For a second agent of one kind, pick another name: `run claude-2 claude`.

`shell-init` prints one shell function per agent. After the user adds `eval "$(node <skill-dir>/agent-mailbox.mjs shell-init)"` to the shell startup file, typing `claude` or `codex` in a repo with this skill runs the agent through `run`. Elsewhere the function starts the plain command. This command never edits the startup file.

## Rules

- Never rewrite or truncate the file. Only the script appends to it.
- Keep credentials and personal data out of the mailbox.
- `inbox` keeps one cursor per sender name, so it never repeats a message. The first call shows the last 20.
- `read` shows the last 20 messages. Use `--all` for the full history.
- `send` with no message reads it from standard input, so a long message needs no shell quoting.
- `watch` is optional. It runs until you stop it. In Claude Code, start it with the `Monitor` tool,
  so a new message wakes the session. If another agent can wake on output from a background
  process, start `watch` there too. Without such a feature, rely on `inbox`.
- No agent starts automatically. The user starts each one.
